lessons.title: Story Time: Old MacDonald Had a Farm
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to join in with and recall a repetitive farm-themed text.
success_criteria: I can join in with the repeated part.
I can name a farm animal from the story.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read/sing a farm-themed repetitive text, modelling joining in and animal sounds.
lessons.independent_task: Children recall farm animals from the text and their sounds, drawing their favourite.
key_questions: What animal is on the farm?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note engagement with repetitive text structure — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Sing the farm song to your family.

lessons.title: Counting Farm Animals to 20
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count and record sets of farm animals to 20.
success_criteria: I can count a set of farm animals.
I can write the numeral.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting farm animal counters into sets, recording numerals.
lessons.independent_task: Children count sets of farm animal counters up to 20, recording numerals.
key_questions: How many animals in this set?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy to 20 — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Count toy farm animals or pictures at home.

lessons.title: Farm Animals and Their Babies
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to match farm animals to their offspring.
success_criteria: I can name a farm animal's baby.
I can match the pair.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce farm animal offspring names (calf, lamb, piglet, foal, chick).
lessons.independent_task: Children match adult farm animals to their offspring, recording the names.
resources_needed: Adult and baby farm animal picture cards
key_questions: What is a baby cow called?

differentiation.greater_depth: Match 6+ pairs and recall names independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note vocabulary and matching skill — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Learn a new baby animal name with your family.

lessons.title: What Is a Farm?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe features of a farm using geographical vocabulary.
success_criteria: I can name a feature of a farm.
I can use a geography word (field, farmyard).
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a farm picture and discuss what's there.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss farm features using geographical vocabulary (fields, farmyard, barn, crops).
lessons.independent_task: Children label a farm picture with key features.
key_questions: What is this part of the farm called?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the purpose of each farm feature

lessons.assessment_notes: Note geographical vocabulary use — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a farm you've visited or seen in a book.

lessons.title: Writing About Farm Animals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write factual sentences about a farm animal.
success_criteria: I can write a fact about a farm animal.
I can use a capital letter and full stop.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a factual sentence about a farm animal.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 factual sentences about a chosen farm animal.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note factual writing progress — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family a fact about a farm animal.

lessons.title: Addition and Subtraction: Farm Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve mixed word problems using a farm context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving mixed word problems using a farm context (e.g. sheep entering/leaving a field).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve farm-themed word problems, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a farm word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Wild Animals: Where Do They Live?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name wild animals and their habitats.
success_criteria: I can name a wild animal.
I can say where it lives.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss wild animals and their habitats (forest, jungle, savannah), contrasting with farm animals.
lessons.independent_task: Children match wild animals to their habitats, recording their matching.
resources_needed: Wild animal and habitat picture cards
key_questions: Where does this wild animal live?
How is this different from a farm?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note habitat understanding — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Look up a wild animal and where it lives.

lessons.title: Farms vs Wild Habitats
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare a farm to a wild habitat.
success_criteria: I can say one difference between a farm and a wild habitat.
I can say one similarity.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing a farm to a wild habitat (e.g. jungle) using a simple comparison chart.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a comparison chart for a farm and a wild habitat.
key_questions: How is a farm different from the wild?

differentiation.support: Complete with adult support, one similarity/difference

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative geographical thinking — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.plenary: Share comparisons made with the class.
lessons.home_link: Compare a farm and a zoo/wild place you've visited.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Farm and Wild Animal Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read farm/wild animal words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read animal words.
I can read a sentence about animals.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending farm/wild animal words (e.g. 'sheep', 'lion', 'goat').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading farm/wild animal words over the week.

lessons.title: Position and Direction: Animal Maze
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to give and follow directional instructions.
success_criteria: I can give a direction instruction.
I can follow a direction instruction.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model giving directional instructions (forwards, backwards, left, right, turns) to move a toy animal through a simple maze.
lessons.independent_task: Children give and follow directional instructions to guide a toy animal through a maze.
key_questions: Did the animal reach the end?

differentiation.greater_depth: Give a full sequence of instructions independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Record position/direction language use — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.home_link: Practise giving directions at home (e.g. to a toy or person).

lessons.title: Tame vs Wild Behaviour
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a behaviour difference between farm and wild animals.
success_criteria: I can describe a farm animal behaviour.
I can describe a wild animal behaviour.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how a farm dog behaves vs a wild fox.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss behaviour differences (farm animals are cared for and tamer; wild animals hunt/forage for themselves).
lessons.independent_task: Children compare a farm and wild animal's behaviour, recording their comparison.
resources_needed: Farm and wild animal picture cards
key_questions: How does this farm animal behave?
How does this wild animal behave differently?

differentiation.support: Compare with adult support, one behaviour

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of domestication vs wild behaviour — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Observe a pet or animal's behaviour at home.

lessons.title: Farm vs Wild Animal Debate
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to state and justify an opinion about farm vs wild animals.
success_criteria: I can say my opinion.
I can give one reason for it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's farm and wild animal learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model stating an opinion with a reason: 'I think farm animals are more interesting because...'
lessons.independent_task: Children state and justify their opinion on farm vs wild animals in a class discussion.
key_questions: Which do you find more interesting?

differentiation.support: Adult provides sentence frame for opinion and reason
differentiation.greater_depth: Respond respectfully to a differing opinion

lessons.assessment_notes: Note ability to state and justify an opinion — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Recap the range of opinions shared respectfully.
lessons.home_link: Discuss with your family which animals you find most interesting.

lessons.title: Ordering Numbers to 20: Animal Race
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to order a set of numbers to 20.
success_criteria: I can order numbers to 20.
I can find missing numbers in a sequence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model ordering scattered numbers to 20 using an animal race theme (animals numbered for a race).
lessons.independent_task: Children order numbered animal cards to 20 and find missing numbers in sequences.

differentiation.greater_depth: Order numbers to 20 and find missing numbers in multiple sequences

lessons.assessment_notes: Record ordering and sequencing skill — evidence for MATHS.N1.

lessons.title: Endangered Wild Animals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe why some wild animals need protecting.
success_criteria: I can name an animal that needs protecting.
I can say one reason why.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the concept of endangered animals simply and sensitively, with an example (e.g. tigers, pandas).
lessons.independent_task: Children draw an endangered animal and record one way to help protect it.
key_questions: Why does this animal need help?
What could people do to help?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain habitat loss reasoning in more detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early environmental awareness — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Talk about an endangered animal with your family.

lessons.title: Farm and Wild Animals Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about farm and wild animals.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about farm and wild animals, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What is a farm animal's baby called?
Why do wild animals need to hunt?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on farm and wild animals you learned about.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Number, Direction, Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply number, direction, and word problem skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can order numbers to 20.
I can follow directions.
I can solve a word problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of the week's number, direction, and word problem learning.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 23 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N1/N2/GEO.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising number ordering over the weekend.

lessons.title: Farming: Then and Now
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe one way farming has changed over time.
success_criteria: I can say one way farming has changed.
I can give a reason why.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a picture of old farm machinery vs modern.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss how farming has changed with technology (hand tools to tractors/machines).
lessons.independent_task: Children compare old and new farming methods, recording one change.
resources_needed: Old and new farming picture cards
key_questions: How did farmers work in the past?

differentiation.greater_depth: Give reasoning for why farming has changed

lessons.assessment_notes: Note change over time understanding, linking history and geography — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Talk about how things have changed on farms with your family.
